subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw keep this issue as the canonical core architecture track for separating the Gateway control plane from per-agent runtime compute, and what first milestone should be sponsored?
rationale: The next step chooses public protocol, config, security, lifecycle, and migration boundaries across Gateway, agents, channels, sessions, and deployment, which automation cannot safely decide.

options.title: Approve Phased Runtime Split
options.body: Keep this as the canonical RFC and start with a local-split protocol, trust model, per-agent lifecycle, and session/delivery migration design before containers or Kubernetes runners.

options.title: Narrow To Execution Placement
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/82017 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/84758 as the active slice while leaving full control-plane separation deferred.

options.title: Defer Core Architecture Change
options.body: Keep supporting multi-gateway/operator workarounds and avoid committing to a distributed runtime boundary until stronger maintainer demand or design capacity exists.

recommendation.title: Approve Phased Runtime Split
recommendation.body: Keep this as the canonical RFC and start with a local-split protocol, trust model, per-agent lifecycle, and session/delivery migration design before containers or Kubernetes runners.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest routing signal from the related worker-runtime experiment and recent agent/gateway history.
